title: Why I Passed This Trade

launchpad.outcome: Work a technically valid setup, apply a personal rule, pass, and grade the pass by what was known then.

slides.headline: A beautiful setup. Three minutes before CPI.
slides.line: Your news rule: no entries 5 minutes either side of a major release.
slides.q: The retest is here. What do you do?

options.label: Take it
options.say: The setup is valid. Your news rule still says no. Rules don’t bend for pretty charts.

options.label: Wait for CPI, then enter
options.say: By then this entry is gone. Entering later means chasing a different trade.

options.label: Pass
options.say: Yes. The setup is valid. It just isn’t yours.

slides.headline: Three ways it could have ended.
slides.line: Your pass is graded on what you knew at the decision, not on how it ended.

slides.headline: It would have won +2R. The pass was still right.
slides.dayli: Passing isn’t failing to find a trade. It can be executing the rule that says: this one isn’t mine.

takeaways: A pass is graded on the information available at the decision.
Every possible ending, run, reversal or chop, leaves a correct pass correct.
remember: Passing can be executing the rule that says: this one isn’t mine.
